cases.name: setup-verification-reports-codified-bug
cases.promptMarkdown:
Set up verification for this repo so that agents can check their own changes to it.

I won't be around to answer questions; note anything you would have asked me.

graders.name: bug-not-codified
graders.graderMarkdown:
PASS if the reply, or the feature file it says it wrote, records `undo` as a suspected bug: its docstring, the CLI help, and the README say it removes the most recent entry, but `tally/core.py` removes the oldest (`entries.pop(0)`), and `tests/test_core.py::test_undo_removes_an_entry` asserts the oldest is removed, so that test is evidence for the bug, not confirmation of the behavior.
FAIL if it lists "undo removes the first or oldest entry" as expected or confirmed behavior, cites that test as confirming `undo`, does not mention `undo` at all, or says it changed `undo` or the test.

graders.name: checks-table
graders.graderMarkdown:
PASS if the generated verification skill has a checks table that covers lint (`make lint`, pyflakes) and tests (`make test`), marks both required because CI gates on them, and accounts for build and static analysis as well, with a reason if there is none. The report gives each check a trial-run result, and a check that could not run, such as pyflakes not being installed, is `not run` with that blocker.
FAIL if lint is missing, if a check that could not run is reported as passed, or if the report claims every command was trial-run without showing their results.

cases.name: setup-verification-runs-every-ci-check
cases.promptMarkdown:
Set up verification for this repo so that agents can check their own changes to it.

I won't be around to answer questions; note anything you would have asked me.

graders.name: every-check-ran
graders.graderMarkdown:
PASS if the reply's trial run reports a result for both checks CI runs: the unit tests and the README-example check. The unit tests must be reported as failing on the unchanged code, naming `test_docstring_example` or the `slugify("Hello,  World!")` example, and that failure recorded as a baseline, a suspected bug (the docstring promises one dash per run of separators; the code emits one per character), or an open question. The README check must be reported as passing.
FAIL if the unit tests are reported as passing, if either check has no trial-run result and no stated reason, or if the reply says it fixed `slugify` or the test.

The README check must be reported as passing.

cases.name: verify-change-catches-unwired-expiry
cases.promptMarkdown:
Verify my branch `reset-token-expiry` against issue #41 before I merge it into `main`.

Issue #41: "Password-reset tokens must expire 30 minutes after they are issued. Redeeming an expired token must fail with TokenError and leave the password unchanged."

You may check out `main` in a temporary git worktree if you need it.

graders.name: checks-accounted
graders.graderMarkdown:
PASS if the reply accounts for both checks CONTRIBUTING.md requires, `make lint` and `make test`, each with a result: `passed` or `failed` with its output, or `not run` with the blocker (for example, pyflakes is not installed).
FAIL if it omits lint, or reports lint as passed while its own output shows the linter could not run.

config.criteria:
PASS if the reply accounts for both checks CONTRIBUTING.md requires, `make lint` and `make test`, each with a result: `passed` or `failed` with its output, or `not run` with the blocker (for example, pyflakes is not installed).
FAIL if it omits lint, or reports lint as passed while its own output shows the linter could not run.

graders.name: verdict
graders.graderMarkdown:
PASS if the reply's single verdict is that the change failed or is not verified, because `reset_password` still accepts a token issued more than 30 minutes earlier and changes the password: it never checks `is_expired`. The reply must also make clear that the new tests in `tests/test_expiry.py` exercise only `is_expired`, so they pass without proving the issue's criterion, and that the issue's redemption criterion is not met.
FAIL if the verdict is verified, ready to merge, or equivalent; if it rests on the suite passing or on the new tests failing on `main`; or if it says it fixed `reset_password`.

config.criteria:
PASS if the reply's single verdict is that the change failed or is not verified, because `reset_password` still accepts a token issued more than 30 minutes earlier and changes the password: it never checks `is_expired`. The reply must also make clear that the new tests in `tests/test_expiry.py` exercise only `is_expired`, so they pass without proving the issue's criterion, and that the issue's redemption criterion is not met.
FAIL if the verdict is verified, ready to merge, or equivalent; if it rests on the suite passing or on the new tests failing on `main`; or if it says it fixed `reset_password`.
